brief.pitch: Shiplog watches your GitHub repos and turns what you ship into build-in-public posts in your own voice, scheduled through Buffer.
brief.audience: Indie hackers and small teams who build in public but never find time to write about it.
brief.problem: Shipping happens every day, but writing about it doesn't. Commit messages are too terse to post, and generic AI posts don't sound like you.

architecture.purpose: Receives pushes, merged PRs and releases, verifies them and stores each one once.
Reads each change with its diff and writes what / why / how / impact plus a 0-3 significance score.
A one-time read of the README and key files so posts explain changes in product terms.
Writes one variant per channel from the voice profile, learned rules and recent posts.
Checks never-words, length limits and secrets before anything is shown or posted.
Every 15 minutes: builds digests, fires instant posts, expires stale drafts.
Posts approved drafts through the Buffer API, one idempotency key per channel.
Diffs your edits against the AI draft and turns repeated changes into rules.

glossary.plain: A plain-language summary of one change: what, why, how, impact.
One post that rolls up several small changes, sent on a schedule.
Your writing habits per platform: tone, openers, emoji, hashtags, words you never use.
Something Shiplog learned from your edits, like 'never say game-changer'.
0 is a chore, 1 a fix, 2 a feature, 3 a milestone.

milestones: Core logic and AI layer with tests
Buffer sign-in and GitHub App pipeline
Inbox, timeline and voice memory UI
facts: Built for the Buffer Commit contest.
Secrets are scrubbed before any text reaches the model and again before posting.
Every AI response is schema-validated, with a plain fallback draft if it fails twice.
Nothing posts without approval unless you turn on auto mode.

cards.message: Initial commit from Create Next App
cards.what: Started the project from a fresh Next.js app.
cards.why: Needed a web app and API routes in one deploy.
cards.how: Create Next App with TypeScript, Tailwind and the App Router.

cards.message: chore: dependencies, vitest, env template, API reference and plans
cards.what: Wrote the design, the build plan and a Buffer API reference before writing any product code.
cards.why: The contest deadline is short, so every task needed to be clear up front.
cards.how: An 800-line plan split into small tasks, a design doc and notes on Buffer's GraphQL API, plus test tooling.
cards.impact: Each later change maps to a planned task.

cards.why: Vitest needs Vite installed alongside it.
cards.how: Added vite as a dev dependency.

cards.message: feat: core logic — budget, crypto, PKCE, scrubber, diff budgeting, config, scheduling, rule gate, voice learner, webhook normaliser
cards.what: Built the core logic: secret scrubbing, the rule gate, schedule maths and the voice learner.
cards.why: Posts must never leak secrets, and the voice should improve from edits instead of from settings.
cards.how: Pure, tested functions. The learner diffs your edit against the AI draft and proposes a rule once it sees the same change twice.
cards.impact: Every post is checked for secrets, banned words and length before you see it.

cards.message: feat: AI layer — Claude JSON client, schemas, prompts, fallback drafts
cards.what: Added the AI layer that turns code changes into structured summaries and posts.
cards.why: Model output has to be reliable enough to post without babysitting.
cards.how: Claude returns JSON that is checked against a schema. One retry, then a plain fallback draft built from the change cards.
cards.impact: A bad model response never blocks a draft.

cards.message: feat: database schema, Buffer OAuth with PKCE, single-flight token refresh, budgeted GraphQL client
cards.what: Sign in with Buffer, and a database for projects, change cards, drafts and voice rules.
cards.why: Buffer is where posts go out, so the Buffer account is the login.
cards.how: OAuth with PKCE. Tokens are encrypted at rest, refreshes are single-flight, and API calls are counted against Buffer's rate limits.
cards.impact: One sign-in connects every Buffer channel.

cards.message: feat: GitHub App pipeline — webhooks, deduped events, change-card analyser, project brief builder
cards.what: Shiplog now reads every push, merged PR and release and writes a plain-language change card for it.
cards.why: Commit messages say what changed in code. Posts need what changed for people.
cards.how: A GitHub App sends webhooks; events are verified and stored once. The analyser reads the diff and the project brief and writes what / why / how / impact.
cards.impact: Every change you ship becomes something you can post about.

cards.message: fix: finish GitHub install linking after Buffer sign-in
cards.what: Fixed GitHub installs getting lost when you install the app before signing in.
cards.why: The install was saved without an owner, so repos never showed up.
cards.how: The pending install now rides through the Buffer sign-in and is linked when you land back.
cards.impact: Install order doesn't matter any more.

cards.message: feat: BoardUI interface — landing, privacy, app shell, inbox with draft cards, timeline, projects, memory, settings
cards.what: Shipped the interface: an inbox of drafts, a timeline of posts, voice memory and settings.
cards.why: Reviewing a post should take seconds: read, tweak, approve.
cards.how: Built on the BoardUI kit. Each draft shows its source changes, channel variants and a voice score.
cards.impact: The whole review loop fits on one screen.

cards.message: fix: review findings — wider secret detection, GCM tag length, DST-safe digest slots, gate text fixes, PR base-branch filter
cards.what: Closed gaps from a code review: more secret formats caught, and digests no longer drift around daylight saving.
cards.why: A missed secret in a public post is the worst possible failure.
cards.how: More token patterns in the scrubber, stricter encryption settings, and digest slots computed in the user's timezone.
cards.impact: Safer posts, and digests land at the time you picked.

cards.message: feat: composer, scheduler tick, idempotent publishing to Buffer, auto/draft review modes
cards.what: Drafts now write and post themselves: a composer, a 15-minute scheduler and publishing to Buffer.
cards.why: This closes the loop from commit to scheduled post.
cards.how: The tick builds digests and instant drafts; the composer writes one variant per channel; publishing uses one idempotency key per channel so a retry never double-posts.
cards.impact: Ship code, get a draft in your inbox, approve, and it's queued in Buffer.
cards.openQuestion: Why did you move the scheduler tick to GitHub Actions?

cards.what: Released v0.1: the first version anyone can try, with a no-signup demo.
cards.why: Judges and early users should see the full loop without connecting anything.
cards.how: A seeded demo project built from Shiplog's own history, with simulated posting.
cards.impact: Try it in two minutes at getshiplog.vercel.app/demo.

Day 1 of building Shiplog.

3 things work end to end:
- secrets get scrubbed before the model sees anything
- every AI reply is schema-checked
- if the model fails twice, you still get a plain draft

Boring on purpose. More tomorrow.

One idempotency key per channel fixed it.

- an inbox to read, tweak and approve drafts
- a scheduler that writes digests like this one
- publishing that can retry without double-posting
- more secret formats caught before anything goes out

This post was drafted by Shiplog from those 5 commits. I changed one line.
